title: What Do People in the Coldest Village on Earth Actually Do All Day?

props.titel: What do people in the coldest village on Earth actually do all day?

scenes.text: What do people in the coldest village on Earth actually do all day? Meet Oymyakon.
Oymyakon sits in the Sakha Republic, in the far northeast of Russia, thousands of kilometres from Moscow. Around five hundred people live here.
On the sixth of February, nineteen thirty-three, a thermometer here showed minus sixty-seven point seven degrees Celsius. That makes Oymyakon the coldest permanently inhabited place on Earth.
But summers can be warm. In July twenty ten, it reached thirty-four point six. The village has seen a swing of more than a hundred degrees.

props.tekst: Cars are often left running all day

scenes.text: In winter, the average is around minus fifty. So cars are often left running all day, because a stopped engine can mean a dead battery.
People wear thick layers of fur and wool. Eyelashes freeze. Even a short walk outside can be dangerous without the right clothes.

props.tekst: Reindeer meat and frozen raw fish

scenes.text: Crops cannot grow here, so the winter diet is mostly meat and fish. Reindeer meat, and a dish of thin frozen raw fish called stroganina.
And school? Reports say the village school only closes when it drops below about minus fifty-two. Children walk there in the dark.

props.label: of darkness a day in midwinter

scenes.text: In midwinter, it is dark for around twenty-one hours a day.
So why does anyone live here? The place began as a stop for reindeer herders, who watered their animals at a spring that never froze.

scenes.text: Life here is hard, but it goes on. Follow Tiny Globe for the next place on the map.
